name: El Salvador
system_note: Power is concentrated in President Bukele.
snapshot: Nayib Bukele's gang crackdown made El Salvador one of the safest countries in the region, at the cost of mass detention and a near-total concentration of power.
culture: El Salvador is Central America's smallest country, and pupusas, thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese or beans, are its national dish, with their own national day. Archbishop Óscar Romero, murdered in 1980 and canonised in 2018, remains a towering figure. Surf Town on the Pacific coast is a tourism showcase.
society: A 1980 to 1992 civil war killed some 75,000. Gangs like MS-13, formed among refugees in Los Angeles, then dominated neighbourhoods until Bukele's state of emergency since 2022 jailed more than 80,000 people, over 1 percent of adults. Murders have fallen dramatically, and Bukele's approval is very high. The US has sent deportees to the CECOT mega-prison.
situation: In 2015 El Salvador was the murder capital of the world, with gangs like MS-13 controlling whole neighbourhoods. Nayib Bukele, a former advertising executive who calls himself the world's "coolest dictator," declared a state of exception in 2022 and has kept it renewed ever since, jailing more than 80,000 people, about 1 in 60 adults, many without trial. Murders collapsed, and Bukele became the most popular leader in the hemisphere. He has used that popularity to remove every limit on his power.

In 2024 he won a second term despite a constitutional ban, after judges his party appointed reinterpreted the rule. In August 2025, his party's legislators, holding 57 of 60 seats, approved indefinite presidential re-election, extended the term to six years and scrapped runoffs (AP via Fox Baltimore). They also cut his current term short by two years, moving the next general election to March 2027, so he can win a longer term sooner. "Democracy in El Salvador has died," said one of the three opposition deputies who voted no. Human rights lawyers and journalists who documented abuses in his prisons, including the anti-corruption lawyer Ruth López, have been arrested or forced into exile (News Central). His mega-prison CECOT, which houses deportees sent by the Trump administration, has made him Washington's most useful ally in the region. In 2026 the country is effectively in campaign season for a vote whose result few doubt.
power: Formally a presidential republic; in practice power is concentrated in Bukele, whose New Ideas party controls the Legislative Assembly, the Supreme Court and the attorney general's office. Constitutional guarantees remain suspended under the state of exception.
